title: Sooji Halwa
subtitle: Semolina roasted in ghee with cashews, cooked in sweetened milk and water until it leaves the pan.
protein: ~5g protein per serving — from semolina, milk and cashews

method.title: Warm the sweet milk
items: In a pan, add {@sugar}, {@water}, {@milk} and {@saffron} if using
Stir and heat on medium until hot and the sugar dissolves — don't let it boil
If using saffron, let it steep 2–3 min for colour
Keep it warm on the lowest flame

method.title: Roast the sooji
items: Meanwhile, put a second pan on medium heat and add {@ghee}; let it melt
Stirring continuously, roast on low-medium heat; add {@cardamom}
Keep stirring 8–9 min, until the sooji is fragrant and just beginning to change colour (roast 1–2 min more for a darker halwa)

method.title: Cook the halwa
items: Add the hot syrup {from Step 1} slowly, in 2–3 parts — it bubbles and splutters a lot, so be careful
Whisk continuously with one hand as the liquid goes in
Keep stirring; the sooji absorbs the liquid and thickens
Stir 2 min more, until the halwa thickens and leaves the sides of the pan

method.label: Toddler — her bowl
items: Scoop {=2–3 tbsp} into her bowl and pick out the cashew pieces (or crush them fine)
Let it cool to just warm — halwa holds heat

method.label: Tip
method.text: This halwa is lightly sweet; use ½ cup sugar for a sweeter one. Less ghee: you can go down to ¼ cup, but not lower, or the sooji won't roast evenly. Stovetop, with two pans side by side — one keeps the sweet milk hot while the other roasts the sooji.
